bib.title: GENERATE RATHER THAN RETRIEVE: LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS ARE STRONG CONTEXT GENERATORS

question: Can a large language model replace the retriever in a retrieve-then-read pipeline by generating contextual documents for a question, and does that match or beat retrieval on knowledge-intensive tasks?
hypothesis: Generated documents contain the correct answer more often and are more question-specific than top retrieved documents, and diversifying generation by clustering-based prompts improves answer coverage and downstream QA.
contributions: A generate-then-read pipeline: prompt an LLM to generate contextual documents instead of retrieving them from Wikipedia or Google.
A clustering-based prompting method that generates multiple diverse documents to raise the chance of covering the correct answer.
Experiments on three knowledge-intensive tasks (open-domain QA, fact checking, dialogue) in zero-shot and supervised settings, matching or beating retrieve-then-read without external documents.

method.summary: text-davinci-002 (InstructGPT, 175B) is prompted to write a background document per question (greedy, zero-shot) and then reads it, or in the supervised setting writes K=10 documents with clustering-based few-shot prompts that a fine-tuned FiD reader (T5-770M or T5-3B) reads. Compared with BM25, Contriever, DPR and Google search documents, and with merged retrieved+generated documents.
method.task: open-domain QA (NQ, TriviaQA, WebQ), fact checking (FEVER, FM2), open-domain dialogue (WoW)

datasets.name: TriviaQA open domain
datasets.split: open test; additional Wikipedia dev split of 7,993 for comparison with GPT-3/GLaM/PaLM
datasets.source: Joshi et al., 2017; splits as Izacard & Grave 2021 / Karpukhin et al. 2020

datasets.name: Human-prompt validation set
datasets.split: validation for 30 student annotators writing generation prompts
datasets.source: random pairs from the three QA datasets
datasets.preprocessing: recall threshold of 50 for an accepted prompt

other.note: FiD-xl runs out of memory above 20 documents on A100 (Fig 3 caption)

models.name: OPT and Codex as alternative generators

training.objective: inferred: standard FiD answer-generation fine-tuning on generated/retrieved documents (paper says only 'fine-tuned on the training split of target datasets')
training.lr: peak 1e-4 (FiD-l; 5e-5 WoW) and 3e-5 to 6e-5 (FiD-xl, per dataset, Table 7); searched 5e-6 to 4e-5
training.batch_size: FiD-l: 64 (16 WoW); FiD-xl: 16 (8 WoW); text also says 16 total for both setups with 1 A100 or 8 A100 at 2 per GPU
training.steps: FiD-l: 15,000 NQ, 10,000 TQA/WebQ/FEVER/FM2, 20,000 WoW; FiD-xl: 20,000 NQ, 15,000 TQA/WebQ/FEVER/FM2, 20,000 WoW (Table 7)
training.hardware: T5-770M: one A100; T5-3B: 8 A100 (2 per GPU)

other.checkpoint_selection: best validation step, then report test (Table 7)
other.text_vs_table_conflict: Text A.2 says 770M uses batch size 16 on one A100; Table 7 upper block (FiD-l) lists total batch size 64.

inference.decoding: greedy decoding throughout the zero-shot experiments; nucleus sampling p=.95 as sampling baseline for multiple documents
inference.samples: one generated document per question in zero-shot; K=10 documents per question in supervised (one per cluster); single run per setting, no seeds stated
inference.prompting: Step 1 generate a background document with an instruction prompt (zero-shot) or with n=5 question-document pairs from one cluster as in-context demonstrations (supervised); Step 2 read with a P3 reading-comprehension prompt
inference.retrieval: baselines: BM25 (pyserini), DPR, Contriever, Google search; 10 documents unless stated; FiD baselines also with 100 documents (published numbers)

parameters.K_clusters: equals the number of documents generated (10 in main results; varied in Fig 2)
parameters.clustering: K-means over GPT-3 embeddings of [question; document] pairs
parameters.initial_document: from the LLM zero-shot, or alternatively BM25
parameters.human_prompts: top-10 of 29 prompts written by 30 students

metrics.name: Exact match (EM)
metrics.definition: answer correct iff its normalized form matches an acceptable answer

metrics.name: Recall@K
metrics.definition: percentage of top-K retrieved or generated documents that contain the answer

metrics.name: Answer coverage
metrics.definition: percentage of all possible answers contained in the 10 documents

baselines: GPT-3, Gopher, FLAN, GLaM, Chinchilla, PaLM
FiD-l and FiD-xl on DPR or Google documents
eval.protocol: Single run per configuration, no significance test or seeds reported; zero-shot Table 1 reports one prompt, v3 adds average over three reading prompts (Table 20).

availability.data: generated documents released at the same repo

prompts.text:
Generate a background document from Wikipedia to answer the given question. 

 {query}

Generate a background document from Wikipedia to support or refute the statement. 

 Statement: {claim}

evidence.quote: We use one A100 for running T5-770M and set the batch size of 16.

results.claim: Supervised, GenRead with clustering prompts and a FiD-xl reader on 10 InstructGPT documents beats DPR-FiD on TriviaQA.
results.setup: TriviaQA open test, text-davinci-002, 10 generated documents, FiD-xl 3B fine-tuned on TQA train
results.note: Abstract's +4.0 is against published FiD-770M with 100 docs (71.6-67.6); against the own 10-doc FiD-xl DPR it is +5.3.

results.claim: Same setup on WebQ also beats DPR-FiD.
results.setup: WebQ open test, FiD-xl, 10 generated documents, clustering prompts

results.claim: On NQ the generated-document reader loses to DPR-based FiD.
results.setup: NQ open test, FiD-xl, 10 generated documents, clustering prompts
results.note: Authors attribute the gap partly to temporal and incomplete-answer labelling issues (A.7).

results.claim: Merging retrieved and generated documents is best on all three QA sets (average EM).
results.metric: average EM over TQA, WebQ, NQ
results.setup: FiD-xl, merged row: TQA 74.3, WebQ 56.2, NQ 54.0
results.quote: it can improve +5.7 averagely on three open-domain QA benchmarks compared to DPR alone, and improve +4.4 averagely compared to the large language model alone.

results.claim: Clustering prompts improve average EM over nucleus sampling when generating the documents.
results.setup: Supervised, FiD reader, 10 documents, three QA sets
results.quote: the clustering-based prompt method can improve the EM score by +2.2 on average

results.claim: Zero-shot, GenRead lifts InstructGPT over its no-document prompt by 6.9 EM on average across NQ, TriviaQA, WebQ.
results.setup: Zero-shot, greedy decoding, text-davinci-002 as generator and reader
results.quote: GENREAD can improve the EM score by +6.9 on three open-domain
results.note: Table 1: NQ 28.0 vs 20.9, TQA 59.0 vs 57.5, WebQ 24.6 vs 18.6.

results.claim: Zero-shot GenRead on NQ is below DPR + InstructGPT but near Google + InstructGPT; DPR is trained on NQ.
results.note: Table 20 averages over three reading prompts; Table 9 on the Wikipedia dev split gives 28.2.

results.claim: Generated documents beat retrieved ones on Recall@1 in TriviaQA.
results.table: Table 10, row GENREAD (clustering prompts), column TriviaQA R@1

results.claim: Answer coverage on NQ is lower for generated documents than DPR documents, because generated documents are less diverse.
results.table: Table 4, row GENREAD (clustering prompts), column NQ

results.claim: Only the largest InstructGPT generator beats DPR-FiD; smaller sizes do not.
results.setup: Ada 150M to Davinci 175B generators, FiD-xl 10 docs, TriviaQA and WebQ; values read from Fig 4
results.quote: Only with the largest size InstructGPT,

results.claim: Other generators also work: Codex scores highest, OPT below InstructGPT but near DPR.
Cost break-even: generating 10 documents with InstructGPT is cheaper in FLOPs than DPR only below about 2473 questions.
results.setup: DPR BERT-base 110M encoding 21M documents once (2.3e17 FLOPs) vs 175B x 10 docs x 55 tokens = 9.6e13 FLOPs per question
results.note: Quote fragment kept short; full statement 'X ≈2473'. FLOPs not a direct measure of cost, per authors.

results.claim: About 16.5% of NQ questions have time-dependent answers; in 100 inspected NQ GenRead predictions, 29 were annotation mistakes (13 temporal, 16 incomplete answers).
results.quote: we found that 29 examples have data collection and annotation mistakes

limits: Authors concede it cannot update knowledge or adapt to new domains without retraining the LLM, unlike swapping documents in retrieve-then-read.
Generated documents can hallucinate (Table 15) and are less diverse than retrieved ones, so answer coverage is lower on NQ.
Only three LLMs tested; conclusions may not hold for other models (Ethics).
Reader uses 10 documents rather than 100 for cost reasons, so the comparison to published 100-document FiD mixes document counts.
NQ underperforms DPR-FiD; authors blame temporality and incomplete labels, supported by a 100-example manual study.
No seeds, variance or significance tests are reported; the dependence on a closed API model (text-davinci-002) hinders exact reproduction.
Possible training-data overlap between the public QA benchmarks and the 175B model is not examined.

terms.definition: first prompts a large language model to generate contextual documents based on a given question, and then reads the generated documents to produce the final answer
cluster question-document embeddings into K classes, sample n pairs from each cluster as in-context demonstrations, and generate one document per cluster
percentage of the number of answers that are contained in the documents over all possible answers
